methods.label: Count grid intervals and diagonals
methods.explanation:
The grid lets us read horizontal and vertical lengths directly. For the slanted strokes, a unit-square diagonal is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with both legs equal to \(1\). By the Pythagorean theorem, its length is
\[
\sqrt{1^2+1^2}=\sqrt{2}.
\]
The letter A has a diagonal consisting of two unit-square diagonals, a vertical stroke of length \(2\), and a horizontal crossbar of length \(1\). Its total length is therefore \(3+2\sqrt{2}\).

The letter M has two vertical strokes of length \(2\) each and two unit-square diagonals. Its total length is \(4+2\sqrt{2}\).

The letter C has three strokes, each of length \(2\), so its total length is \(6\).

Adding the lengths of all strokes gives
\[
(3+2\sqrt{2})+(4+2\sqrt{2})+6
=13+4\sqrt{2}.
\]
The answer is \(\boxed{13+4\sqrt{2}}\) units, choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
